newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crudes remain pricey for U.S. buyers.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crudes remain pricey for U.S. buyers.

text.p: Foreign crude grades remained expensive which kept trading into the U.S. market thin on Monday, market players said.

The premium for prompt physical Brent eased in London, trading down from an 11 cent-a-barrel premium over November forward Brent paper to as low as two cents above, but outright prices continued to firm.

Current front-month December was up around 10 cents a barrel at $25.60/bbl late in the London day. Trades in the 'window' in the U.S. lifted that level to between $24.75 and $24.80 and Dated Brent was up by a similar amount.
West Texas Intermediate November tracked the outright gains in Brent but the premium remained narrow at around 60 cents, too thin a margin to encourage trans-Atlantic sales.
Traders said crudes from Nigeria and Latin America also remained firm.
"There is so little Brent-related coming this way that WTI-related are still a good buy," said a Houston-based trader of foreign crudes.

Traders said the Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol was rumored to have sold another Cusiana cargo for November 21-25 loading, at a 35-cent premium to January WTI, the same premium as last week. Also rumoured, an end-November loading Argentinian Mendanitos cargo sold by YPF at WTI -$1.35 fob.
"The buyer (of last week's Cusiana) is offering that out again 'cause he thinks he can get a better price," said one trader.

Meanwhile, traders said West African grades also were bid up, with three Qua Iboe cargoes selling to the state Indian Oil Corp for mid-November lifting at premiums to Dated Brent of between $1.17 and $1.25.
That compares with spot trades last week slightly above 80 cents above Dated Brent for late November delivery.
